title: Close the tenant permission-isolation defect cluster: role-key global namespace, missing tenant dimension on data-scope policies, and the broken self-service onboarding chain
goal: The 2026-10-19 tenant delivery acceptance ran 193 assertions on a live multi-tenant stack and passed 179 (92.7%), leaving 13 defects of which 5 are P0. Those 5 P0 are not five independent bugs but one defect cluster in three layers: `role_key` is treated as a cross-tenant global namespace. `system_role`, `system_role_permission` and `system_role_data_scope` all already carry `tenant_id` and a `(tenant_id, role_key)` unique key, yet half of the read/write paths degrade to role_key-only, and the write path drops the tenant value into `tenant_id = 0`. Proven consequences: a tenant admin sees 53 roles in the data-scope console while owning 3; the same admin can write a data-scope policy for a role that exists only in another tenant; and flipping one policy from `self` to `all` widened another tenant's ordinary user from 1 visible row to 3, in both directions. This program moves tenant scoping from the table definition into the read/write paths, and closes the remaining 8 P1/P2 from the same acceptance run. Delivered in seven waves: W0 contract plus red tests, W1 data-scope tenant dimension (F7/F8/F9/F10/F11/F13), W2 tenant user onboarding and membership (F1/F4), W3 role-menu grant persistence (F3), W4 session revocation and login gate (F2), W5 console UX (F5/F6), W6 re-verification and closeout.
findings: F1 (P0, tenant self-service onboarding is broken): POST /system/user succeeds and the user shows up with dept and roles, but login returns 403 tenant.forbidden because CreateUser writes only system_user and never a tenant_memberships row; GateSessionIssuance requires an active membership.

F2 (P1, 16-minute lockout after credential changes): RevokeUserTokens sets the user-level blacklist key blacklist:<userID> with TTL AccessTokenTTL+1m, and login never clears it, so a password reset or a disable/enable cycle keeps every new session rejected with 401 token.expired.force.

F3 (P0, tenant role navigation grants are lost): rbacbind.InsertRoleMenus inserts system_role_menu without tenant_id, so grants land on tenant_id=0 while loadRoleMenus reads under the tenant scope; the grants are unreadable, and re-saving an existing tenant role deletes the rows it then fails to rewrite.
F4 (P2, ghost memberships): deleting a user leaves its tenant_memberships row active, so the tenant member list keeps showing __deleted_user_* entries.

F5 (P1, two 403 toasts on every console page): TenantViewpointSwitcher proxies platform capability with hasPerm('system:tenant:list'), which a tenant admin holds because it owns the full console key set, so it calls GET /system/tenant/list and gets 403 tenant.platformOnly on every page load (twice under StrictMode).

F6 (P1, department tree renders only the root): DeptList binds the nested tree to the table with pagination.total = data.length and no expandable/childrenColumnName, so Arco Table renders the root node only and reports a total of 1.

F7 (P0, data-scope console lists other tenants' roles): ListDataScopePolicies queries system_role with only `deleted_at IS NULL` and no tenant predicate, so tenant A's console shows 53 rows while A owns 3 roles, including a role key that exists only in tenant B.

F8 (P0, cross-tenant data-scope write succeeds): UpdateDataScopePolicy validates the role through ensureRoleKeyExists, which only checks that the role_key exists in ANY tenant; tenant A successfully wrote a policy for a role that exists only in tenant B and got code 200.

F9 (P1, policy writes lose the tenant dimension): UpdateDataScopePolicy builds PermissionRoleDataScopePolicy without assigning TenantID and declares OnConflict on role_key alone, so the row lands on tenant_id=0 while the role module writes the correct (tenant_id, role_key) row for the same key.

F10 (P0, one tenant can widen another tenant's visible data): the middleware's SystemRoleDataScope struct has no TenantID field, loadRoleDataScopePolicies filters on role_key only, and resolveDataScopeMode returns all if any matching row is all; setting the shared key to all raised tenant B's user from 1 visible row to 3, and the reverse direction behaved identically.

F11 (P1, custom deptIds are not tenant-validated): UpdateDataScopePolicy accepts any dept_id and stores it verbatim; tenant A submitted tenant B's department 203 and it was persisted, while dept_id is a global sequence whose values collide across tenants.

F13 (P1, role list echoes another tenant's dataScope): RoleService.loadRoleDataScopes queries system_role_data_scope by `role_key IN (...)` with no tenant predicate, so the last scanned row wins; tenant B's role showed self in its own list while its stored policy was all.

F14 (P2, cross-tenant role reads return 500): GET /system/role/:id/users, /user-candidates and PUT /system/role/:id return code 500 request.failed instead of 404/403 when the role belongs to another tenant, which makes authorization probes look like service failures.

Redesigning the five data-scope modes (all / self / dept / dept_and_children / custom)
Changing the Casbin domain-subject naming rule role:<key>@tenant:<id>, which is already correct
Introducing isolation mechanisms beyond row-level tenant_id (schema-per-tenant, database-per-tenant)

implementationNotes: Contract first: TENANT_CONTRACT_V1.md §2.3 currently only says tenant-scoped resources carry tenant_id; it does not say read paths must filter by it and write paths must assign it. W0 adds that clause so every later wave is reviewed against a written rule instead of a convention.

tenant_id = 0 means the platform/global scope, not unknown. Every new predicate must distinguish three cases explicitly: platform scope (tenantID == 0 from a platform subject) passes through; tenant scope (tenantID != 0) filters hard; missing context fails closed rather than falling back to all.

DataScopeMiddleware is the hot path for every data-scope-governed request. Preserve the fail-closed semantics (rolePoliciesCoverAll denies when a role has no row) and add unit tests that two tenants holding the same role_key each read only their own row.

Migrations stay idempotent and reversible: follow 000021 (INSERT IGNORE + LEFT JOIN, down writes a comment only). Backfill only unambiguous rows where a role_key exists in exactly one tenant; duplicated keys are resolved by an operator with the inspection SQL from the acceptance report §5.6, because guessing an owner is worse than not guessing.

F2's clear point is a security boundary: the user-level blacklist may only be cleared after successful authentication, never on arbitrary requests, and session-level revocation must survive so old refresh tokens stay dead.

Both frontend defects are wrong decision inputs, not styling: F5 proxies platform capability with a permission key the tenant admin legitimately holds, and F6 hands a nested tree to a table that was never told to render children.
Do not touch pkg/tenant/authz.go or pkg/database/scope.go: the domain-subject construction and the row-narrowing hook are correct; the defect is what gets fed into them.

graphFocus: every authorization-table read/write path must answer where the tenant comes from

executionRoles.implementerPosture: Advance wave by wave; each wave is an independently reviewable change set; red before green (W0 lands failing cases first). Before editing any SQL, answer where that query's tenant comes from.
reviewerPosture: Check every new or modified authorization-table SQL for a tenant predicate, or an explicit justification that it is platform scope.
Re-assert fail-closed: a missing policy row must deny, never fall back to all.
Check that tenant_id = 0 is never used as 'unknown' and that platform scope is not written into tenant scope.
Check migrations are idempotent, reversible, and never guess an owner during backfill.
Check the blacklist clear in F2 happens only after successful authentication and that session-level revocation still rejects pre-change tokens.
Check both frontend fixes correct the decision input rather than swallowing the error toast.
